In [[algebraic geometry]], given a [[line bundle]] ''L'' on a [[smooth variety]] ''X'', the '''bundle of ''n''-th order principal parts''' of ''L'' is a vector bundle of rank <math>  \tbinom{n+\text{dim}(X)}{n} </math> that, roughly, parametrizes ''n''-th order Taylor expansions of sections of&nbsp;''L''.

Precisely, let ''I'' be the ideal sheaf defining the [[diagonal embedding]] <math>X \hookrightarrow X \times X</math> and <math>p, q: V(I^{n+1}) \to X</math> the restrictions of projections <math>X \times X \to X</math> to <math>V(I^{n+1}) \subset X \times X</math>. Then the bundle of ''n''-th order principal parts is<ref>{{harvnb|Fulton|1998|loc=Example 2.5.6.}}</ref>
:<math>P^n(L) = p_* q^* L.</math>
Then <math>P^0(L) = L</math> and there is a natural [[exact sequence]] of vector bundles<ref>{{harvnb|SGA 6|1971|loc=Exp II, Appendix II 1.2.4.}}</ref><!-- need to cite EGA and SGA 3 as well -->
:<math>0 \to \mathrm{Sym}^n(\Omega_X) \otimes L \to P^n(L) \to P^{n-1}(L) \to 0.</math>
where <math>\Omega_X</math> is the sheaf of differential one-forms on ''X''.

== See also ==
*[[Linear system of divisors]] (bundles of principal parts can be used to study the osculating (as in [[osculating plane]]) behaviors of a linear system.)
*[[Jet (mathematics)]] (a closely related notion)
